# opencode-openspec-status — contributor guide

A **read-only** OpenCode TUI plugin: it draws in the sidebar where the project
stands in its OpenSpec (SDD) or ODD flow, plus the gentle-ai review when there is
one.

## Layout

- `src/model.ts` — type contract between layers. No IO.
- `src/i18n.ts` — `en` and `es` messages, `t(key, params)` and locale detection.
  Every user-visible string goes through it; add each new key to both locales.
- `src/sources/` — pure parsers for `sdd-status`, `review status`,
  `review-state.json`, `odd/tasks/*.md` and git, plus the file readers. They
  produce a `Snapshot`. `openspec-files.ts` infers the `sdd-status` JSON from the
  OpenSpec files when gentle-ai is not installed.
- `src/view/` — `Snapshot` → `FlowView` → lines of `{ text, color, bold }`
  segments (sidebar ≤ 38 columns, full screen, compact indicator). No IO.
- `src/runtime/` — `run.ts`: the real `Run` (argv without a shell, `isAllowed`
  allowlist before every spawn, 5 s timeout, 2 MB cap, executable lookup with a
  fallback PATH); `poller.ts`: per-source polling without overlaps, last value
  plus `stale`; `activity.ts`: the open session's activity (`api.state.session`:
  status, questions and permissions) and since when it has been working.
- `src/tui.tsx` — only draws: the OpenCode slots and the `/openspec-status` route.
  The only file that depends on the OpenCode plugin API.
- `test/fixtures/` — gentle-ai 3.7.0 outputs (anonymized) and synthetic ones
  marked `synth`.

## Commands

- `bun install` — dependencies.
- `bun run check` — typecheck + tests. Run it before calling anything done.
- `bun test` — tests only. The suite runs with the Spanish locale (`test/setup.ts`);
  `test/view/english.test.ts` covers English.

## Rules

- **Read-only.** The plugin may only run `gentle-ai sdd-status`,
  `gentle-ai review status` and `git --no-optional-locks status`, and read files.
  Never `review start`, `capture-*`, `recover`, `sdd-continue` or anything that
  changes state, even if a JSON carries the command ready to run. The only write
  is the pin (SDD change or ODD feature), set with Enter in `/openspec-status` or
  by the plugin when new work starts in the session (`origin: "new"`,
  `src/runtime/new-work.ts`), in OpenCode's KV (`api.kv`, key
  `openspec-status:pin:<real root>:<session>`, one per session); never in
  gentle-ai or the project.
- `gentle-ai review status` runs `git init` if the folder is not a repo: only
  call it when `<root>/.git` exists.
- gentle-ai is optional: a missing executable raises `CommandNotFoundError`; SDD
  falls back to the files and the review is hidden. Any other failure marks the
  source stale.
- No emoji in the UI (they take two columns): use thin box drawing ┌─┐ and
  ●◉○✓✗▸▼◀. Text coming from outside may carry them (✅ ⏳, CJK): always measure
  with `displayWidth` from `src/view/text.ts`, never `.length`.
- In opentui `<span>` has no typed `fg`: each segment is a `<text>` inside a
  `<box flexDirection="row">`.
- The TUI plugin API is not in the public docs: read
  `node_modules/@opencode-ai/plugin/dist/tui.d.ts` (1.18.33).
- Repository files can be hostile. Read them only with `fsx.readText(path,
  { maxBytes })` and the caps in `exec.ts` (regular files only, never blocking on
  a FIFO); never a direct `readFile`.
- Linear parsers: no regexes with overlapping quantifiers (`\s+(.*?)\s*$`,
  `[...]+$`, `Math.min(...list)`); split with `splitLines` and use the caps in
  `src/sources/markdown.ts` (2 KB line, items, text). See `hostile.test.ts`.
- Children are spawned with `childEnv`: PATH with absolute entries only and
  `core.fsmonitor=false`; in their own process group so the timeout kills
  grandchildren too.
- Containment with real paths (`isInside` in `exec.ts`, resolves links and
  /tmp → /private/tmp), never only lexical, before reading paths gentle-ai gives.
- The parsers also recognize Spanish headings and marks (`Tareas`,
  `Siguiente paso`, `(parcial)`…): keep both languages when touching them.
- Bun sometimes creates `bun.lockb` with mode 0777: keep it at 644.
- English in docs, comments and commits (Conventional Commits).

# opencode-openspec-status

A read-only [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) TUI plugin that draws, in the right
sidebar, where your OpenSpec (SDD) change or ODD feature stands and what comes
next.

Spec-driven workflows are easy to lose track of: which phase am I in, is the
agent still writing the spec or waiting for me, did someone touch the specs after
the tasks were written? This plugin answers that at a glance, as a flow diagram,
without running anything that changes state.

![Sidebar with an SDD change in apply](docs/img/sidebar-apply.png)

A guide with screenshots and a technical walkthrough lives in
[`docs/index.html`](docs/index.html).

## Features

- **SDD (OpenSpec)**: the 8 phases (explore → propose → spec → design → tasks →
  apply → verify → archive) as a flow diagram, with the current phase
  ("you are here"), the next one, the apply task progress, the apply/verify loops,
  blocked phases and a warning when an earlier artifact changed after a later one
  (for example, specs edited after `tasks.md` was written).
- **ODD**: the `odd/tasks/<feature>.md` document of the current branch, or the
  newest one with pending tasks; its protocol (authorize → explore → tasks →
  implement → close), the current task, the per-task cycle code → checks →
  commit → review and the next step. Marked **inferred**, because it is deduced
  from markdown and git.
- **Review**: the state of `gentle-ai review status`, its risk, the four lenses
  (risk, resilience, readability, reliability) and whether the review is for the
  current code.
- **Live phase**: the sidebar also reads the open OpenCode session, so it can tell
  "writing spec 1:24" (the agent is working on it) from "waiting for you" (the
  agent stopped or is asking).
- **Prompt indicator**: `SDD · spec ▸ design`, `SDD · apply 6/16 · 1:24`,
  `ODD · T7/9 · rev ✗`…
- **`/openspec-status`**: a full-screen view with an interactive SDD detail
  (browse changes and phases, read proposal, requirements, decisions, tasks and
  verify results, see the linked Azure DevOps or Jira work item) and an overview
  with every ODD feature.
- **Works with or without [gentle-ai](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai)**.
  With gentle-ai installed, SDD status comes from `gentle-ai sdd-status` and the
  review section is shown. Without it, the same status is inferred from the
  OpenSpec files in `openspec/changes/` (header marked "inferred") and the review
  section is hidden.
- **English and Spanish UI**, picked from your locale.

## Requirements

- OpenCode **1.18.x** (TUI plugin API `@opencode-ai/plugin` 1.18.33). OpenCode 2
  uses a different plugin API; see [OpenCode 2](#opencode-2).
- [Bun](https://bun.sh), which OpenCode already uses to load plugins.
- Optional: `gentle-ai` on the `PATH`, and `git`.

## Install

Clone the repository and install its dependencies:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mjtc1985/opencode-openspec-status.git
cd opencode-openspec-status
bun install
```

Add the absolute path of the folder to the `plugin` array of
`~/.config/opencode/tui.json`:

```json
{ "plugin": ["/absolute/path/to/opencode-openspec-status"] }
```

To try it without touching your global configuration, put that same content in a
separate file and point OpenCode at it; plugins listed there are added to the
global ones:

```sh
OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG=/path/to/tui-test.json opencode <project>
```

## Usage

Open OpenCode in a project that has `openspec/changes/` or `odd/tasks/`. The
sidebar shows the diagram on its own; with nothing active it shows the SDD chain
muted and how to start.

Type `/openspec-status` for the full-screen view:

| Key | SDD detail | Overview |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `↑` `↓` | previous / next change | previous / next ODD feature |
| `←` `→` | previous / next phase | |
| `PgUp` `PgDn` | scroll the panel | scroll the diagrams |
| `home` `end` | first / last phase | |
| `enter` | pin the change for the sidebar (again to release) | pin the feature |
| `tab` | switch to the overview | switch to the SDD detail |
| `esc` | back | back |

### Language

The UI follows `OPENSPEC_STATUS_LANG` (`en` or `es`), then `LC_ALL`,
`LC_MESSAGES` and `LANG`, then the system locale. Any Spanish locale shows
Spanish; anything else shows English.

### Which change, which feature

With several active SDD changes the sidebar shows one, chosen in this order:

1. **Pinned**: the one you pinned with `enter` in `/openspec-status`, while it is
   still active and you are on the branch where you pinned it.
2. **Branch**: the change whose work item (`feature/1187-…` → `AB#1187`, or a
   Jira key) matches `workItem:` in its `.openspec.yaml`, or whose name appears in
   the branch name. A work item beats a name; among names, the longest wins.
3. **Recent**: the change with the most recently modified file.

ODD follows the same idea: the feature whose file name appears in the branch, if
it has pending tasks, otherwise the newest one with pending tasks.

When there is both an SDD change and an ODD feature, the sidebar focuses on one
methodology (the pinned one, else the branch's, else the newest) and leaves a
muted `also: …` line for the other. The header says why: `(1 of 6 · branch)`,
`(recent)`, `(pinned)`.

A change or feature **started during the session** is pinned automatically and
marked `new`, so the sidebar jumps to what you just began. Only creation counts:
editing, archiving or switching branches does not trigger it.

Pins are stored per session in OpenCode's TUI key-value store (`api.kv`), under
`openspec-status:pin:<project real path>:<session id>`. That is the only thing the
plugin writes.

### When each mark changes

A phase counts as done when its file exists (the agent creates it when it starts
writing). To tell "writing" from "done, waiting for you", the plugin also reads
the session state:

- **✓** the phase has its file (proposal, specs, design, tasks.md,
  apply-progress, verify-report).
- **◉ writing 1:24**: the agent is working and that phase's artifact is the last
  one touched, less than 3 minutes ago.
- **waiting for you** (yellow): the agent is asking, needs a permission, or
  stopped with a next phase ahead.
- **⚠ changed after …**: an earlier artifact changed more than 5 minutes after a
  later one.

Everything is reread every 3 seconds.

## Read-only by design

The plugin only runs these commands, as argv (no shell), checked against an
allowlist before every spawn:

```
gentle-ai sdd-status [<change>] --json --cwd <root>
gentle-ai review status --cwd <root>
gentle-ai review status --cwd <root> --contract=gentle-ai.review-integration/v2 --next-transition=true --lineage=<lineage>
git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain
```

Never `review start`, `capture-*`, `recover`, `sdd-continue` or anything else that
changes state, even when a gentle-ai JSON suggests the command. Besides that it
reads files: `openspec/changes/**`, `odd/tasks/*.md`, the lineage's
`review-state.json` inside `<root>/.git`, and `.git/HEAD` and `.git/config` for
the branch and the work item.

`gentle-ai review status` runs `git init` in folders that are not repositories, so
the plugin only calls it when `<root>/.git` exists.

Repository files are treated as untrusted: reads are size-capped, only regular
files are read (a committed FIFO cannot block the TUI), paths are checked with
their real location before reading, and every parser is linear.

### Polling

- SDD, ODD and git every 3 s; review every 10 s. Never two reads of the same
  source at once.
- Each command has a 5 s timeout (the whole process group is killed) and a 2 MB
  output cap.
- When a source fails, its last value stays on screen with a
  `stale · <source> failed N s ago` line, until it reads fine again.

## OpenCode 2

OpenCode 2 is opt-in (`opencode upgrade --major`) and ships a new plugin API
(`@opencode/plugin`, `Plugin.define`, slots such as `sidebar.content`). Plugins
written for 1.x do not load there. This release targets OpenCode 1.x; OpenCode 2
support is planned as a second, thin adapter in this same repository, since
everything below `src/tui.tsx` (sources, view model and renderer) does not depend
on the OpenCode API.

## Development

```sh
bun install
bun run check    # typecheck + tests
```

The project layout and the rules for contributors (human or agent) are in
[`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md).

if you distribute a modified version, it must stay under the same license with
its source code available.

# Mobile contact bar and home hero CTA

## Objective

Raise contact rate on mobile by keeping the contact options in sight.

## Problem

Most mobile visitors never scroll far enough to see a phone number or a chat
  link. The landing page with a contact button in the hero converts twice as
  well as the home page.

## Why

Contact is the only conversion that matters for the site.

## Scope (authorized)

- A fixed bottom bar on mobile with two buttons: Chat and Call, with their own
  element ids so analytics can tell them apart.
- A contact button in the home hero, styled like the landing page one.

## Constraints

- Do not click the live links during verification: it would log fake contacts.

## TDD

Off. Source: no project configuration. Runner: none (manual checks).

## Tasks
- [x] T1 Mobile contact bar (route: inline; one non-trivial resource, snippet #36)
- [x] T2 Home hero CTA (route: inline; mechanical copy of the landing page button
      into the home page)
- [x] T3 Record both changes in `analytics/data/changes.yaml` (done inside the T1 and
      T2 commits, one entry each, so every commit carries its own record)

## Acceptance criteria

- The bar shows on mobile only, at the bottom, both links correct, ids present.

## Progress / evidence

- T1: ✅ bar live, ids present.
- T2: ✅ hero button live.

## Next step

Measure after one full week: chat_contact and phone_contact by link_id bar_chat / bar_call, and home contact rate. Push and merge of feat/mobile-contact-bar are the owner's decision.

# Design

## Context

El módulo de precios llama al servicio de tarifas en cada petición.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Reducir las llamadas al servicio de tarifas.

**Non-Goals:**
- Caché distribuida entre instancias.

## Decisions

### 1. Caché en memoria por instancia
- **Decisión**: un mapa con expulsión LRU dentro del proceso.
- **Razón**: no añade infraestructura.

### 2. Clave compuesta región y producto
- **Decisión**: la clave es `region:producto`.

### 3. Invalidación por evento de censo
- **Decisión**: escuchar el evento de publicación y vaciar por región.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- **[Precios desfasados entre instancias]** → cada instancia tiene su caché.
  *Mitigación*: TTL corto por defecto.
- **[Consumo de memoria]** → muchas regiones por muchos productos.
  *Mitigación*: límite de entradas con LRU.

## Migration Plan

1. Desplegar con la caché desactivada.
2. Activarla por entorno.

# Proposal

## Why

Cada consulta de precio llama al servicio de tarifas, que responde en cientos de
milisegundos y limita las peticiones por minuto. En picos de tráfico el listado
de productos se degrada.

Una caché por región y producto evita repetir la misma consulta dentro de su
vigencia.

## What Changes

- Caché en memoria de precios con clave por región y producto.
- **TTL configurable** por entorno (`PRICE_CACHE_TTL`), con valor por defecto
  de cinco minutos.
- Invalidación al publicar un censo nuevo de tarifas:
  - por región afectada;
  - completa si el censo es global.
- Métricas de aciertos y fallos de caché.
- El cliente de tarifas pasa a reintentar con espera exponencial.
- Documentación operativa del parámetro nuevo.
- Límite de memoria con expulsión LRU.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `price-cache`: caché de precios por región y producto con TTL e invalidación.

### Modified Capabilities
- `pricing-api`: el endpoint de precios lee de la caché antes que del servicio.

## Impact

- **Código**: módulo de precios y cliente de tarifas.
- **Configuración**: variable `PRICE_CACHE_TTL`.

# Propuesta

## Por qué

Las cantidades de la orden de montaje pierden decimales al convertir unidades.
Hay pedidos de ejemplo como el de calle-real-34 y la referencia OM-2291 del
almacén que muestran el redondeo.

## Qué cambia

- Conversión de unidades con aritmética decimal.
- Redondeo solo al presentar, nunca al guardar.

## Capacidades

### Capacidades nuevas
Ninguna.

### Capacidades modificadas
- `order-units`: conversión decimal de cantidades.

# Tareas

## 1. Conversión

- [ ] 1.1 Sustituir la aritmética de coma flotante
- [ ] 1.2 Pruebas con cantidades fraccionarias

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Servir precios desde memoria mientras sigan vigentes.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Clave de caché por región y producto
El sistema SHALL guardar cada precio con la clave compuesta región y producto.

#### Scenario: Acierto de caché
- **WHEN** se pide un precio ya guardado y vigente
- **THEN** se devuelve sin llamar al servicio de tarifas

#### Scenario: Región distinta
- **WHEN** se pide el mismo producto en otra región
- **THEN** se trata como una clave distinta

### Requirement: Vigencia configurable
El sistema SHALL descartar las entradas con más antigüedad que el TTL.

#### Scenario: Entrada caducada
- **WHEN** una entrada supera el TTL
- **THEN** la siguiente consulta va al servicio de tarifas

### Requirement: Invalidación al publicar censo
El sistema SHALL vaciar las entradas afectadas al publicar un censo.

#### Scenario: Censo regional
- **WHEN** se publica un censo de una región
- **THEN** solo se vacían las entradas de esa región

#### Scenario: Censo global
- **WHEN** se publica un censo global
- **THEN** se vacía toda la caché

#### Scenario: Publicación repetida
- **WHEN** el mismo censo se publica dos veces
- **THEN** la segunda publicación no cambia nada
